problem: VLN agents trained with behavioural cloning only optimise the per-step conditional action distribution P(a|s), so errors compound along trajectories. RL-based alternatives need hand-crafted rewards and are unstable for transformer VLN models, and DAgger-style fixes still only match the conditional policy.
motivation: Matching the expert's full state-action occupancy measure should align the whole trajectory with the expert instead of single-step decisions. An energy-based model can represent this joint distribution flexibly without a tractable partition function, and it can be plugged into existing VLN architectures.
key_idea: Reinterpret the VLN policy as an energy-based model of the joint state-action distribution P(s,a) with E(s,a) = -action logit, and train it with cross-entropy plus a marginal state likelihood term estimated by SGLD sampling from a persistent Marginal State Memory.
insight: The joint objective is equivalent to minimising the forward KL between the expert's and the agent's occupancy measures, which gives global trajectory alignment beyond BC. The ablation shows that removing the state-marginal term L_S (leaving only L_pi, i.e. BC/DAgger) drops DUET R2R val SR from 74 to 72 and VLN-BERT R2R val SR from 65 to 61. Gains are largest on long paths (about 5-6% SR for paths over 16 m) and on path fidelity (NDTW on RxR-CE), which fits the global-alignment story. Compared with AIRL (reverse KL), ENP does slightly better (R2R-CE val SR 45 vs 43) and avoids adversarial training.
method: Energy parameterisation: models P(s,a)=exp(-E(s,a))/Z, with the energy set to the negative action logit, E(s_t,a_k) = -a_t[k], so the existing action classifier serves as the energy function.

Loss factorisation: -log P(s,a) = -log P(a|s) - log P(s); L_pi is the standard cross-entropy (BC) and L_S is the marginal state matching loss, with P(s) obtained by marginalising over the K action candidates.
Gradient estimation of L_S: the gradient is grad E(s) - E_{s_hat~P}[grad E(s_hat)]. The negative samples s_hat come from SGLD in the state-representation space with step size 1.5 and noise N(0,0.01).

Marginal State Memory: a replay buffer of size 100 that persists MCMC chains (persistent contrastive divergence). SGLD is initialised from the buffer with 95% probability and from uniform noise otherwise. The buffer is filled during pre-training and reused in finetuning to cut the iterations needed.
DAgger-style data aggregation: rollouts of the current policy are labelled with expert shortest-path actions and mixed with the original data.

Plug-in usage: the policy learning of EnvDrop, VLN-BERT, DUET and ETPNav is replaced with ENP, keeping their original hyper-parameters. SGLD iterations are I=15 for EnvDrop and VLN-BERT, and I_pre=20, I_ft=5 for DUET and ETPNav. Inference is unchanged, so there is no extra test-time cost.
Theory: the objective is shown to be the forward KL between occupancy measures (mode-covering), contrasted with BC's conditional KL and AIRL's reverse KL.

setting.backbone: EnvDrop (LSTM Seq2Seq), VLN-BERT, DUET and ETPNav (transformers), each retrained with ENP
setting.training_data: Standard benchmark expert demonstrations for R2R, REVERIE, R2R-CE and RxR-CE, with each base model's original training recipe (EnvDrop back-translation augmentation, PREVALENT augmentation for VLN-BERT, pre-training plus finetuning for DUET and ETPNav). No new extra data.
setting.observation: Panoramic RGB with candidate views (plus depth and a waypoint predictor in continuous environments), topological map history
setting.action_space: Discrete panoramic candidate viewpoints / topological graph nodes; waypoint predictor in CE
setting.privileged: Expert (shortest-path) action queries during training only (DAgger-style); none at test time

results: ENP improves every base architecture it is plugged into, though the gains are small. On R2R test unseen, DUET goes from 69 to 71 SR and VLN-BERT from 63 to 65 SR. On REVERIE val unseen, DUET improves by 1.92 SR and 2.59 RGS. On R2R-CE test unseen ETPNav goes from 55 to 56 SR, and on RxR-CE val unseen from 54.79 to 55.27 SR and from 61.90 to 62.97 NDTW. It still trails map-augmented methods such as BEVBert, BSG and VER on R2R and REVERIE.
limitations: Gains over strong baselines are small (about 1-2% SR), and ENP is only tested on four architectures.
SGLD inner loops add training cost (about 9% delay for 5 iterations) and need tuning of hyper-parameters such as I, step size and noise.
Safety and collision avoidance, and dynamic real-world environments, are not addressed; evaluation is simulation-only.
